conceptual assets.information: The enable setting determines whether the timer operates, whether counting and interrupt generation proceed, and whether the downstream clock generator is enabled.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: An unchecked bus write changes the enable bit at line 76, which controls the clock-enable output and timer and interrupt operation at lines 106, 118, and 141. Clearing the enable through line 76 disables clkgen_en_o at line 106, resets the count at lines 118-119, and clears interrupt state at lines 147-149.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker issuing a bus write to the control register could clear the enable bit and disable timer operation and interrupt generation.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler setting selects which generator timing source advances the timer and therefore determines the timer's operating rate.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Bus writes modify the prescaler bits at lines 77-79, and those bits select the timing source used to produce timer.tick at line 117. An altered selection can withhold or excessively delay timer advancement because timer.count advances only when timer.tick is asserted at lines 120-125.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a prescaler value that selects an unsuitable or inactive timing source and thereby stall or distort timer events.

conceptual assets.information: The threshold setting determines the count value at which the timer matches, resets its count, and produces a pending interrupt.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: An unchecked bus write replaces timer.thres at line 84, and the threshold participates in the match decision at line 131 that controls count reset and interrupt generation at lines 121-145. Changing the threshold can defer or withhold the timer event because it determines when the match and interrupt occur at lines 131-143.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write an extreme threshold value to delay or effectively suppress the timer interrupt.

conceptual assets.information: The timer count is the elapsed-time state on which timer operation and threshold matching depend; it is generated and updated internally and returned on a bus read.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The count is reset or updated by enable, tick, and match-controlled logic at lines 119-124, so bus-controlled settings can alter its evolution and value. Clearing the enable stops normal counting and resets the count at lines 118-120, preventing the timer from progressing.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could change the enable or threshold settings to reset or mis-time the counter and prevent the timer from reaching its intended event.

conceptual assets.information: The match decision indicates that the timer count equals its threshold and selects the next timer and interrupt actions. It is computed internally from timer state and configuration and has no direct entry or exit port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The count-versus-threshold comparison is computed at line 131 and directly selects count reset and interrupt assertion at lines 121-145, so changing its inputs can produce an incorrect decision. Preventing the match decision can defer the count reset and withhold the interrupt selected by lines 122 and 143.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the threshold or timer operation so that the match decision occurs at the wrong time or does not occur when required.

conceptual assets.information: The pending interrupt state records that the timer event has occurred and drives both the interrupt output and the interrupt-status read-back bit.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The pending state is set, cleared, or forced low by the match, clear command, and enable controls at lines 141-149, and is observable through irq_o and bus read-back at lines 94 and 154. An attacker could clear or suppress the pending state through the control and clear paths at lines 81 and 144-149, withholding the interrupt.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue an interrupt-clear or disable write to remove a pending timer interrupt before the receiving system observes it.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt-clear command requests removal of the pending timer interrupt and is registered internally before it is applied.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The bus write data supplies the clear command at line 81, which is registered in irq_clr and used to clear irq_pnd at lines 144-145, so an unauthorized command can alter interrupt state. The same clear path can remove the pending indication before irq_o is observed at line 154, withholding the interrupt.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write the interrupt-clear bit while an interrupt is pending and suppress notification to the rest of the system.
